topic: Eye injury first aid: chemical splash = rinse with clean water, don't rub, go to hospital

youtube.title: Chemical splash in the eye? Don't rub! 🚿 First aid #Shorts
youtube.description:
Something splashed in your eye? Don't rub. Here's what to do in the first minute.
கண்ணில் ரசாயனம் பட்டால்: தேய்க்காதீர்கள், உடனே தண்ணீரில் கழுவுங்கள்.

• Rinse immediately with clean running water for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelids open.
• Remove contact lenses if they come out easily.
• Don't rub. Don't put oil, milk or home remedies in the eye, and no drops unless a doctor says so.
• If something hit the eye or is stuck in it: don't press, don't pull it out, cover gently with a paper cup.
• After rinsing, go straight to an eye hospital or emergency, and take the chemical bottle with you.
• Prevention: cleaners out of children's reach, goggles for strong chemicals, and care with lime (sunnambu).
• General education only, not a substitute for emergency care.

gmb.text: Eye first aid every home should know. If a chemical such as floor cleaner or lime splashes into the eye, don't rub. Rinse immediately with clean running water for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelids open, and remove contact lenses if they come out easily. Don't put oil, milk, home remedies or any drops in the eye unless a doctor advises it. If something hit the eye or is stuck in it, don't press and don't pull it out; cover it gently with a paper cup. Then go straight to an eye hospital or emergency, and take the chemical bottle with you. Keep cleaners out of children's reach and wear goggles for strong chemicals.
